**Applies To**: All AI assistants | **Generated by**: NAOS Portable Governance Kit

## Quick Reference

| Rule | Summary | Rule posture |
|------|---------|:-----------:|
| 1 | Update existing files, never create new ones | 🔴 blocking |
| 2 | No archive folders (use `git rm`) | 🔴 blocking |
| 7 | **Evidence-First Analysis** — Verify before assuming, search before creating | 🟡 advisory |
| 10 | **License Review** — copyleft-risk dependencies require explicit project approval | 🔴 blocking |
| 11 | **Anti-Duplication** — Search before creating any new function or file | 🟡 advisory |

> **Quickstart = 3 blocking-posture + 2 advisory rules.** Labels are policy posture,
> not executable-check counts. Hook source defines commit checks and has no licence
> scanner; init does not install `license-scan.yml`. The broader gate defaults to `warn`.
>
> Want more? Compare Lite with `naos upgrade . --tier lite --dry-run` (no apply).

## Rule 1: Update Existing Files 🔴 blocking

```
FORBIDDEN: docs/analysis_2025-XX-XX.md, notes/session_summary.md, draft_*.md
REQUIRED: Update existing docs (STATUS.md, CHANGELOG.md, README.md)
```

**Generated-hook boundary**: hook source defines the archive, backup, session,
root temp/draft, and dated-analysis patterns; other examples remain review posture.

**Exception**: `docs/exploration/` is exempt for exploratory work.

**Exception (Story Cards)**: Creating/updating story cards under your active task directory
is allowed to support the governed workflow.

**If new file needed**: Justify in commit message why no existing file is suitable.

---

## Rule 2: No Archive Folders 🔴 blocking

```
FORBIDDEN: */archive/
REQUIRED: git rm path/to/obsolete_file.md
```

Git history IS the archive. Never create `archive/`, `old/`, or `backup/` directories.

---

## Rule 7: Evidence-First Analysis 🟡 advisory

Before making decisions, verify with real data. This is the simplified 3-principle version
of the full Deep Analysis Protocol (available in Governance Lite and above).

### The 3 Core Principles

| # | Principle | What It Means |
|---|-----------|---------------|
| 1 | **Evidence-First** | Never assume — validate with real data on actual project files |
| 2 | **Exhaustive Impact Search** | Find ALL affected files, not just the obvious ones |
| 3 | **Verify Claims at Source** | Don't trust README/marketing. Check actual behavior |

### When to Apply

- **Any dependency change**: Verify license, test on real project data
- **Any bug investigation**: Find ALL occurrences before fixing
- **Any code change**: Search for all affected files before editing

### Minimum Checklist

```
[ ] Tested on real project data (not assumptions)
[ ] Found all affected files (grep/search across codebase)
[ ] Verified claims at source (licenses, actual behavior)
```

> **Full protocol**: Lite; compare with `naos upgrade . --tier lite --dry-run` (no apply).

## Rule 10: License Review — Copyleft-Risk Approval 🔴 blocking posture

Copyleft-risk dependencies require source verification and explicit project approval;
obligations depend on use and legal context. This is not legal advice.

### The Rule

```
EXPLICIT REVIEW: AGPL, GPL, LGPL, EUPL, MPL, CDDL, EPL, and unknown/custom licences
COMMON DEFAULTS: MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, ISC, PSF-2.0, CC0-1.0
```

### How to Verify

```bash
# Before adding ANY new dependency:
pip show <package> | grep License    # Python
npm info <package> license           # Node.js
go-licenses check ./...              # Go
```

### Execution Boundary

The hook does not scan licences and init does not install `license-scan.yml`.
Rule 10 is review posture unless an adopter validates another consumer.

[ADAPT: If your project is itself GPL-licensed, relax this rule to allow GPL dependencies
and document the project-specific review/enforcement decision.]

## Rule 11: Anti-Duplication — Search Before Creating 🟡 advisory

**Before creating ANY new function, class, or utility**:

1. Search the codebase for existing implementations:
   ```bash
   grep -r "def function_name" src/      # Python
   grep -r "function functionName" src/   # JavaScript/TypeScript
   grep -r "func FunctionName" .          # Go
   ```

2. Search for semantic equivalents (functions that do the same thing with different names):
   ```bash
   grep -r "similar_keyword" src/
   ```

3. If a similar function exists, **extend or reuse it** instead of creating a duplicate.

### Why This Matters

AI assistants are the #1 source of duplicate functions in codebases. They can't see
sibling modules three directories away. Without this rule, you'll find 4 config loaders,
3 date formatters, and 2 HTTP clients — all created by AI in separate sessions.

### The Discipline

```
BEFORE creating: Search. Read existing code. Understand what's already there.
IF similar exists: Extend, refactor, or reuse.
ONLY IF truly novel: Create a new function with a clear, non-overlapping name.
```

> **Full anti-duplication tooling**: Standard; compare with
> `naos upgrade . --tier standard --dry-run` (no apply).

## What's NOT in Quickstart (and Why)

| Capability | Available In | Why It's Not Here |
|------------|-------------|-------------------|
| Spec-driven development | Lite+ | Requires spec templates + task registry |
| Agent coordination | Lite+ | Requires agent definitions + handoff templates |
| Cognitive checkpoints | Lite+ | Requires checkpoint skill + memory protocol |
| Function Index tooling | Standard+ | Requires index generator + pre-commit integration |
| Semantic duplicate detection | Standard+ | Requires embeddings + similarity threshold config |
| Behavioral compliance testing | Standard+ | Requires autoresearch runner + scenario battery |
| Full traceability matrix | Standard+ | Requires RTM generator + spec alignment enforcement |
| Truth validation | Assured | Requires governance truth table + canonical metrics |

**Rule 26 / PAUL context brackets.** Quickstart does not enforce cognitive
checkpoints. In Lite and higher, Rule 26 asks agents to pre-declare the active
PAUL bracket for each checkpoint: FRESH (>75% headroom), MODERATE (35-75%),
DEEP (25-35%), or CRITICAL (<25%). DEEP requires compacting before new
sub-tasks; CRITICAL requires stopping, saving a full checkpoint, and handing off
via `strategic-compact` before continuing.

**Existing-project comparisons (existence-only; no apply)**:
```bash
naos upgrade . --tier lite --dry-run
naos upgrade . --tier standard --dry-run
naos upgrade . --tier assured --dry-run
```
